question: Which body parts are mainly inflamed in gastroenteritis?
explanation: Gastroenteritis means inflammation of the lining of the stomach and intestines. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h1)

question: What is the biggest risk for a patient suffering from gastroenteritis?
explanation: Frequent vomiting and watery diarrhea quickly drain body water and electrolytes, leading to dehydration. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h1)

question: Which virus is the most common cause of severe diarrhea in babies?
explanation: Rotavirus attacks the lining of the intestines, causing severe watery diarrhea in infants and toddlers. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h2)

question: An outbreak of profuse rice-water stool diarrhea points strongly to which organism?
explanation: Cholera toxin produced by Vibrio cholerae causes the gut to secrete massive amounts of water and salts, creating rice-water stools. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h2)

question: How are most gastroenteritis germs usually spread?
explanation: Germs from waste pass to a new host through contaminated food, water, or unwashed hands. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h3)

question: How do bacterial toxins cause diarrhea in the intestines?

options.A: Triggering massive fluid and electrolyte secretion
options.B: Destroying the liver parenchyma cells completely
options.C: Blocking all blood flow to the large bowel
options.D: Inducing rapid production of red blood cells

explanation: Toxins force the intestinal lining to dump large amounts of water and salts into the gut. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h3)

question: Which physical sign helps spot dehydration in a sick infant?
explanation: The soft spot on an infant's head dips inward when fluid levels drop significantly. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h4)

question: A patient with severe diarrhea has a weak pulse and low blood pressure. What does this suggest?
explanation: Losing too much body fluid drops blood pressure and makes the heart struggle to pump enough blood to organs. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h4)

question: Which test is best for finding a bacterial cause of diarrhea?
explanation: Culturing a stool sample grows the bacteria in the lab and shows which antibiotics will kill it. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h5)

question: Why do nurses check electrolyte levels in patients with severe vomiting and diarrhea?

options.A: To diagnose underlying primary respiratory disease
options.B: To measure the exact bacterial load in the blood
options.C: To detect dangerous imbalances like low potassium
options.D: To evaluate liver enzyme production rates

explanation: Loose stools and vomiting drain essential minerals like sodium and potassium, which must be replaced. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h5)

question: What is the first-line treatment for mild dehydration from gastroenteritis?
explanation: Oral rehydration salts use a special sugar-salt balance to help the gut quickly absorb lost fluids. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h6)

question: Why are antibiotics not used for every case of diarrhea?

options.A: Most cases are viral and antibiotics do not kill viruses
options.B: Antibiotics stop oral rehydration salts from working
options.C: Antibiotics always cause immediate permanent kidney failure
options.D: Bacteria never cause diarrhea in tropical environments

explanation: Viruses cause most stomach bugs, so antibacterial drugs will not help and can cause resistance. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h6)

question: What life-threatening problem can happen if severe dehydration is left untreated?
explanation: Losing too much fluid volume causes a dangerous drop in blood pressure and poor blood flow to organs. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h7)

question: A recovering patient has muscle weakness and heart palpitations. Which electrolyte is likely low?
explanation: Potassium is lost in watery stool, and low levels affect how nerves and muscles, including the heart, work. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h7)

question: What is the most effective public health way to stop the spread of tummy bugs?

options.B: Isolating infected patients in dark rooms
options.C: Handwashing with soap and safe water

explanation: Washing hands stops germs from passing to food, water, and surfaces. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h8)

question: How does exclusive breastfeeding protect an infant against gut infections?

options.A: Preventing the infant from developing any teeth early
options.B: Providing maternal antibodies that boost infant gut immunity
options.C: Creating an impermeable physical barrier in the stomach
options.D: Destroying all bacteria present in the local water supply

explanation: Breast milk contains protective antibodies that help shield a baby's digestive system from harmful germs. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h8)
